I can never get behind these kind of soul-searching expeditions, for lack of a better way to put it.

Every time I read about one it's riddled with the signs of someone who thought they knew what they were doing and still didn't quite get it. It sounds as though he barely made an effort to get to know his co-workers outside of work, and the fact that he obviously had the option to just get up and head somewhere that he would deem "better" has rendered his effort fruitless.

At least his friends had the right idea. Noah clearly took this up for the novelty even if he himself isn't aware of that. Needing a job like this and wanting a job like this are two very different things. I wish him the best of luck for the future, but if he were to ever try again I'd recommend he takes a trip somewhere where that education doesn't matter, and your skill is judged by the thickness of the callouses on your hands.

My immediate reaction to this soul-searching was pretty vomit-inducing, and it feels incredibly exploitative of the working poor.

Pardon me for not knowing the quote verbatim, but in *Good Will Hunting," Matt Damon accuses Minnie Driver of only dating him so that she can tell her rich friends that she "went slummin', too, once" And the fact that he's making money off of this by publishing a story just drives that point home even more, because as soon as he does that, then it wasn't just for the experience, it was for financial gain.

Yes, it is the same as on Wii U. As you are holding shield on a platform, you move the circle pad down fast enough not to just angle your shield and slow enough not to do a spot dodge.

Shadow of the Colossus. Mostly because it was the first difficult game I completed on my own and its art style is truly amazing.

Chrono Trigger. Why? Well... it's a bit of a story, but I made a vid about it here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=twjwRMVXKi4

The original Sly Fox.

Metal Gear Solid 1 & 2. Two moreso than one. I was 14 when MGS2 came out and I was addicted to it, can't tell you how many times I beat it.
Super Mario 64, played with my dad every night before I went to bed for years :)

Mario Kart 64. I used to rush over to my Aunts house to play her Nintendo 64. It was the only game I ever had the chance to play for a large portion of my early childhood and I am still in love with it today.

Hmm, there's a few that I would put in my top for sure. Kingdom Hearts, Pokemon Yellow, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater, Mario Golf GBA, Kaboom (2600), Tiger Woods 2004, Mario Party 2-3-4, Sonic Adventure 1 and 2, Crazy Taxi...

Steel Panthers. Pretty much taught me what games were all about. I still play it's "modernized" versions.

Toy Story 2 for the PS1.

First day of kindergarten. "Hey do you like video games?" "Yeah!" "I like Toy Story 2" "No way me too!"

Best friend till this day. 15 years later.
Probably Command & Conquer Red Alert or the original Shadow Warrior. I've spend so many hours playing those games

Ducktales then Shadowgate were the next games I got. I remember my cousin and I playing Shadowgate and getting stuck at the skeleton king. We ended up writing a letter to Nintendo power to ask for help. We got a response a week later with instructions on how to complete the room. I wish I had the letter still. :(

Donkey Kong Country 2. The music is some of the best videogame music ever made and the later levels are made more immersive by the soundtrack (i'm thinking bramble blast.) As far as SNES there was not a better platformer imo.

The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time

I grew up playing that game for hours upon hours. It's a classic that never gets old for me. I had never owned a console before the N64, so I couldn't get into any of the classic SNES games.
Mine is an old 2600 game called Megamania...used to play it on an old black and white TV with my dad. I'd love to get a copy of that one day...
Secret of Mana on SNES. It was the first game that really immersed me. I'd love to see a revamp for PC one day, or even an MMO-style game be developed.
The original Deus Ex. It was the first game I bought on my Mac G4 back in 2000. It had all the elements of a good FPS, skill sets you had to build up and an interesting complex story.

The Sly Cooper series along with Pac-man World 2.

As I kid I would always play those with my cousins when we were in Mexico visiting. I even remember one summer how we kept trying to beat the original Sly game in one sitting because none of us had a memory card yet. As for Pacman, I remember how excited I was after I would beat a boss after trying for a few days on and off and discovering what the next world would look like.

Good times.
Sonic the hedgehog, Sega mega-drive. Up,down,left,right,A,start.... Sigh

Quest for Glory, it was the first graphical RPG I played that really got me sucked in. The story worked well and it had puzzles, it had so many great components of adventure, action and RPG games and for the early 90s it was pretty damn impressive.

Man, I played the Quest for Glory series to absolute death when I was a kid. I got the 4 game anthology and just loved the crap out of it. The first one especially. I think I replayed it a dozen times.

I remember when the 5th one came out, and it just felt off. Not sure why.

Zombies Ate My Neighbors. We bought because the box looked interesting. Little did we know that little cartridge contained 55 levels of pure, psychosis inducing rage.

That dam spider. I COULD NEVER GET PAST THE SPIDER.

I'm still bitter.

For me it was Baldurs Gate 1. It took ages to install from a stack of CDs but in the end it was well worth the wait. Someone then told me about the experience cap removal patch and that made it even better!
Drone racers, a shitty lil lego licensed racer developed by pre-corrupt EA that got me into the genre in it's entirety.
Planescape Torment because it is the best story ever told in gaming history .
Runescape, I played it as a kid and it was absolutely enthralling then. Still had fun when I fired it up a year ago, although a lot has changed there.

Wing Commander Privateer. My friend and I would take turns playing for hours. That was the first open universe game I played.

Later, I got way into Freelancer.
Metroid 2 or FFVIII. Goldeneye as well, obviously, but those two are the tops.

Serious Sam. It's the first game I remember playing. I remember I played it at my uncles house first when I was real little and I would sit on his lap and work the movement keys while he shot stuff. Still can't get enough of that game.

Doom 1 & 2. I was always a big videogame dork but those games were by first real gaming obsession. I'd fantasize about being a space marine killing Imps and Cyberdemons.

At first all I had was the shareware copy of Doom 1. It was only the first episode but I played it every day, over and over to the point I wasn't doing homework and I got in trouble constantly for it.

Then came Doom 2 and I played that even more. I knew every map, secret, enemy and what weapon worked best to kill them. One day I was at Costco with my dad and I saw a big fat book called "Tricks of the Game Programming Guru's" and it was all about how to make Doom maps. I was never much of a book reader but I read that thing cover to cover repeatedly as I made my own Doom levels. Wish I still had some of those but they're gone forever.
Mario Kart DS, it was my first video game ever and I played it for hours by myself and with friends. Lots of good memories.
The original Spyro or Crash Bandicoot games for PS1. Good times, man.
Final Fantasy IX. First game I completed as a kid over and over. Also, having a crush on Princess Garnet may have helped....

Diablo 1 and 2, 1 because it was the first game I would play online with my cousin. That moment when I first encountered the Butcher is something I will never forget, I had a giddy moment every time I saw a unique item drop. 2 is because I sunk so many damned hours into that game, runewords were so awesome, farming Mephisto and Baal for hours upon hours and still not getting anything worth a damn yet still enjoying tearing shit up with a group of people I met on the internet, ahhhh those were the days.
A friend and I were talking about this the other day. Soldat or Little Fighter. We had a blast playing those back in the day.

I suppose Wolfenstein 3D. I still have the 2 low-density floppy disks, and my original receipt from CompUSA from 1994, $59.95 before tax...I bought it after playing the shareware version I found on a BBS if I'm not mistaken. Forget you filthy map/radar having casuals, I had to memorize where I was/came from. :)

Crystalis.

I would spend hours and hours playing this game, just grinding on mobs and enjoying the chiptune soundtrack. I would finish it, put it away for a month, then come back for a fresh playthrough. I did this for YEARS until I sold my NES to my sister who was going away for college. I really regret that decision, now.
Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic.... My first experience with a game with a story/heart like that.... I really feel like I earned my light-saber in that game...so good

The Legend of Zelda on the NES. My grandmother was very much my mother as my actual mother was always busy working, or out partying, either way. I would watch her play Zelda all the time, and she got me into the game when I was old enough to be able to properly would the controller. She would let me play on her save file, and just smiled at my enjoyment, even if I died a lot.

She would pick up every new game that came out and show me all the tricks and neat things she had learned about it so I could better succeed when I played.

She's since passed on, but it's a game series that will always have a special place in my heart.
